steps.tx: **Intradialytic hypotension**, abbreviated as **IDH**, defined by a **systolic blood pressure** drop of at least **20** mmHg or mean arterial pressure decline of at least **10** mmHg with symptoms, occurs in **15%** to **20%** of maintenance hemodialysis sessions. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: An excessive **Ultrafiltration rate**, or **UFR**, exceeding **13** mL/kg/h independently induces subclinical **myocardial stunning**, transient cerebral ischemia, and mesenteric hypoperfusion, accelerating cumulative cardiovascular mortality in maintenance hemodialysis patients. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients. Structured clinical management and regular follow-up help guide therapeutic optimization and prevent disease complications.

rows: Extend treatment duration or add ultrafiltration sessions

steps.tx: **Dialysis disequilibrium syndrome**, or **DDS**, is a neurological emergency during initial dialysis in patients with severe azotemia and BUN exceeding **150** mg/dL. It is driven by **reverse osmotic** fluid shifts precipitating acute **cerebral edema**. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: Effective **prevention of DDS** when initiating hemodialysis requires limiting treatment duration to **2.0** to **2.5** hours, keeping **blood flow rate** low between **150** and **200** mL/min, and targeting a gentle **urea reduction** of **30%** to **40%**. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

nodes.label: Limit run time to 2.0 to 2.5 hours
Restrict blood flow rate to 150 to 200 mL/min

steps.tx: A **Type A first-use** hypersensitivity reaction occurs within minutes of initiating hemodialysis, mediated by IgE against **ethylene oxide** sterilant or **AN69** dialyzer membranes in patients taking **ACE inhibitors**, requiring immediate circuit clamping without returning blood. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Type A Reaction (Anaphylactic)
points: Onset: Within first 5 to 20 minutes of treatment
Mediators: IgE to ethylene oxide or bradykinin via AN69/ACEi
Clinical presentation: Dyspnea, bronchospasm, urticaria, hypotension
Emergency action: Immediately clamp circuit; NEVER return blood

right.title: Type B Reaction (Nonspecific)
points: Mediators: Alternate complement pathway activation (C3a, C5a)
Clinical presentation: Chest tightness and vague back pain
Action: Supportive therapy; session can typically continue

steps.tx: **Type B first-use** reactions manifest **20** to **40** minutes into hemodialysis with chest and back pain driven by **complement activation** generating **C3a** and **C5a** upon blood contact with bio-incompatible dialyzer membranes. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

rows: High incidence of Type B back and chest pain
Negligible risk of Type B reactions

steps.tx: **Dialysis-related amyloidosis** is caused by systemic deposition of **beta-2 microglobulin** amyloid fibrils in patients undergoing long-term hemodialysis for over **10** years, classically presenting with bilateral **carpal tunnel syndrome** and subchondral bone cysts. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.
steps.say: Dialysis-related amyloidosis is caused by systemic deposition of beta-2 microglobulin amyloid fibrils in patients undergoing long-term hemodialysis for over 10 years, classically presenting with bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome and subchondral bone cysts. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Dialysis Amyloidosis Features
points: Dialysis duration: Typically requires > 8 to 10 years on hemodialysis
Skeletal findings: Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome and bone cysts
Definitive therapy: Renal transplantation halts progression

right.title: Preventive Strategies
points: Membrane selection: High-flux biocompatible synthetic dialyzers
Water purity: Ultrapure dialysate to suppress chronic inflammation
Early transplantation: Timely allograft placement before osteoarthropathy

steps.tx: **Acquired cystic kidney disease**, or **ACKD**, develops in **50%** of patients on hemodialysis for **3** years and over **80%** after **10** years, carrying a **6**-fold increased risk of **renal cell carcinoma** requiring regular surveillance. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.
steps.say: Acquired cystic kidney disease, or ACKD, develops in 50% of patients on hemodialysis for 3 years and over 80% after 10 years, carrying a 6-fold increased risk of renal cell carcinoma requiring regular surveillance. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

rows: Biennial renal ultrasound or contrast CT/MRI
Annual ultrasound to detect papillary or clear cell RCC
